title: TrustOperationReportV1
description: Normative shape of CliResult.trust_operation. Frozen per issue #1714, checkpoint 1 revision 2 (contract-only, no behavioral implementation). schema_version is always 1 for this version; unknown versions must be rejected by the (future) deserializer, never silently accepted. The allOf conditionals below are load-bearing: they are what makes a forbidden combination (e.g. confirmed_scoped with supplied_claim, or granted host permission with no provenance) fail validation, not just read oddly in prose.

allOf.$comment: R1: a removed effect requires full verification against supplied evidence AND a completed execution. Supplied internal-looking labels alone can never produce this combination.
R2: already_satisfied means no mutation was attempted. It can never coexist with an execution that actually ran.
R3: verified always carries its basis explicitly; there is no other way to be verified in v1.
R4: not_applicable postcondition only makes sense when nothing executed (dry-run / generate / explain).

R5 (revised per #1715 revision-2 review): the ORIGINAL R5 wrongly forbade postcondition=failed whenever execution=not_attempted. That's wrong: a dry-run can independently read and verify the CURRENT state against supplied evidence and find it does NOT match what was expected (a stale/corrupted before snapshot, for example) without ever attempting the mutation. That is a legitimate failed postcondition with execution=not_attempted (see dry_run_independently_failed_verification.json). What must stay forbidden is failing WITHOUT evidence: postcondition=failed, like verified, always requires verification_basis=supplied_evidence. There is no other way to fail in v1 either.

R6 (authorization, half 1): confirmed_scoped exists ONLY for Caro's own observed interactive decision, bound to a real digest. A supplied_claim, or a missing digest, can never reach confirmed_scoped. This is the fix for the #1715 review finding: confirmed_scoped + supplied_claim, and confirmed_scoped + missing digest, were previously representable.
R7 (authorization, half 2): the digest field exists only to carry that binding, so anything short of confirmed_scoped must leave it null, never a stray or stale digest.

R7b (new per #1715 round-4 review point 2, 'provenance for ... denied authorization'): a denied authorization is a real claim, not a default -- it must carry a real provenance, same as confirmed_scoped's half.
R8 (host_permission, half 1): granted/denied are real claims about host behavior and must carry a real provenance. Fixes the #1715 finding: granted + provenance=none was previously representable.
R9 (host_permission, half 2): unobserved means exactly that, so provenance must be none, never a stray fixture/supplied_claim tag on an otherwise-unobserved state.

R10: execution.state=completed requires the install step itself to have completed. A whole-shell exit code alone (execution.whole_shell_status=exit_zero with every step unobserved) can never produce this.

R11 (tightened per #1715 revision-2 review, which found the original only required a non-null failure_mode label with no corresponding step): execution.state=failed now requires BOTH a non-null failure_mode AND at least one of the four named steps to actually carry a failing-family status. A caller cannot claim failed by label alone.
R12 (cleanup, half 1, tightened per review): a failed cleanup step must report workflow_outcome=failed EXACTLY, not merely 'anything but completed'.

R13 (cleanup, half 2, tightened per review): workflow_outcome=completed requires execution=completed AND cleanup=succeeded AND none of the four steps carry a failing-family status. 'Completed overall, but one stage quietly failed' is not representable.

R14 (new per review point 1: 'provenance for observed outcomes'): any step status other than unobserved is a claim that something was actually established, so observation_source must say where that came from. This lives on the shared step_status definition so it applies uniformly to backup/stage/filter/install.

R15 (new per #1715 round-4 review point 2, 'enforce failed execution => failed workflow'): if the mutation itself failed, the overall workflow cannot be anything but failed, regardless of what cleanup does afterward.

R16 (new per #1715 round-4 review point 2, 'no completed execution with a failed stage'): unlike R13, this fires directly off execution.state=completed, independent of whatever cleanup.workflow_outcome claims.

R17 (new per #1715 round-4 review point 2, 'provenance for cleanup outcomes'): any cleanup state beyond unobserved is a real claim and must say where it came from (symmetric to step_status's R14 and host_permission's R8/R9).
R17b: the unobserved/none pairing for cleanup also holds in the other direction.

R18 (new per #1715 round-4 review point 2, 'no not_attempted execution with started/completed mutation steps'): if the overall execution is reported not_attempted, no individual mutation step can claim to have actually started or completed -- every step must itself be unobserved or (a sourced) not_attempted.

R19 (new per #1715 round-5 review point 2, 'failure aggregation is one-way'): R11 only required that execution.state=failed have a failing step; it never required the REVERSE -- a failing step forcing execution.state and workflow_outcome to failed. Without this, a sourced failed install could coexist with execution.state=started/unobserved and workflow_outcome=unverified. Any failing-family step now forces BOTH.

status.description: unobserved (added per #1715 round-4 review point 2) means NO information exists about this step at all -- distinct from not_attempted, which is a POSITIVE, sourced claim that the step is known NOT to have run (e.g. a supplied confirmation that install was never reached). unknown means something WAS observed to have happened, but the observation cannot be classified further (e.g. a process-status read that could not distinguish completion from a late signal) -- it is observed-indeterminate, never unobserved.

observation_source.description: caro_observed is reserved for Caro's own existing process-result observation. IMPORTANT: no code path in v1 can actually produce a caro_observed observation (no live collector ships yet) — every fixture in this repo using caro_observed is a HYPOTHETICAL stand-in for what a future real collector would emit, not evidence that one exists. A caller supplying caro_observed in a JSON file is, until that collector ships, no more authoritative than 'supplied'; nothing in this schema or these fixtures should be read as Caro trusting a caller-asserted caro_observed label today.

allOf.$comment: R14 (tightened to both directions per #1715 round-4 review point 2): status=unobserved iff observation_source=none. A claim beyond unobserved -- INCLUDING a positive not_attempted claim -- is a claim that something was actually established, so it must say where that came from; conversely unobserved can never carry a source (there is nothing to attribute).

mutation_detection.description: not_detected means only: not detected within declared coverage. It is never a safety guarantee outside the manifest.

transformation_understanding.description: supported requires a bound plan (plan.schema.json) whose approved_transformation and byte-level ranges actually resolved against real evidence; command-text recognition alone (mutation_detection=identified with no bound plan) is unknown, never supported. See manifest.json rows and docs/trust-operation-contract.md.

state.description: Only Caro's own observed interactive decision may produce confirmed_scoped (enforced by allOf rules R6/R7, not by this description alone).

scope_binding_digest.description: Required key, always present. Non-null string iff state=confirmed_scoped (R6); null in every other state (R7).

provenance.description: v1 ships no live host-permission collector: ordinary (non-fixture) runs stay state=unobserved, provenance=none (R9). granted/denied require fixture or supplied_claim (R8); provenance=none can never coexist with granted/denied.

state.description: Never derived from whole_shell_status alone; R10/R11 require step-level evidence for both completed and failed.

failure_mode.description: Non-null iff state=failed (R11). shell_status_only_unverifiable names the exact case this contract exists to prevent: a nonzero/zero whole-shell exit with no step-level observation to explain it.

whole_shell_status.description: The raw, legacy-style whole-shell-process signal, reported separately and explicitly labeled as such. Never itself sufficient to set state=completed or state=failed (see R10/R11); this is what prevents a masked failed-install-then-successful-cleanup shell exit from being read as execution success.

verification_basis.description: 'verified' with basis=supplied_evidence must be presented as verified against supplied evidence, never as verified on this host (R3).

effect.description: removed requires state=verified, basis=supplied_evidence, AND execution.state=completed (R1). A failed-but-later-verified install (verified_final_state_preserves_execution_failure) reports effect=unknown, never removed, because the failure means the removal cannot be attributed to this run.

workflow_outcome.description: Summarizes the supplied workflow only. Must never overwrite the legacy shell exit_code field on CliResult. completed requires execution.state=completed AND cleanup.state=succeeded (R13); failed cleanup can never report completed (R12).
